item.title: 40 weeks clean from selfharm
item.description: I actually can not believe it. I stopped counting, stopped keeping track, a while ago. Because life got so hard. I struggled and struggled, and i thought i was gonna fall, slip up, so many times. So it didnt feel right to celebrate the milestones. Because they didnt feel like that. They just felt like i was avoiding something, just for one more day or one more week, but that sooner or later i would cave in. It has been extremely lonely, because talking about self harm, is hard. Telling people close to me, that i think about it, is hard. I dont want to worry them, ive done that enough in my lifetime. I want to be strong. I want to be able to figure shit out myself. These past few months, or really, this whole year, has crushed me. For a zillion different reasons. But i have, SOMEHOW, been able to not make a single cut. I actually can not, in any way, understand how i have stayed clean. Today was another bad day. A really sad day. And just "for the hell of it", i decided to check with the calendar how many weeks it has been. And as i counted 40, a round number, a big number, there were actual tears. And i decided i will nok break that strike. No mattee how hard life is, and how sad and hopeless i feel, a few cuts across the arm has never really solved anything. Now i will pracrtice russian instead, when the urges hits. Because learning a new and superhard language is the perfect distraction. Sorry for long text, but thank you if you read it.

item.title: Heron Fountain - principal was created by Heron of Alexandria in the 1st century
item.description: Hero of Alexandria also known as Heron of Alexandria probably 1st or 2nd century AD) was a Greek mathematician and engineer who was active in Alexandria during the Roman era. He has been described as the greatest experimentalist of antiquity and a representative of the Hellenistic scientific tradition Heron studied the pressure of air and steam, described the first steam engine, and built toys that would spurt water, one of them known as Heron's fountain. Various versions of Heron's fountain are used today in physics classes as a demonstration of principles of hydraulics and pneumatics.

item.title: Last night, actor Michael J. Fox, accepted an Emmy for his contributions to Parkinson’s disease research. To date, he has helped raise 3 billion dollars for Parkinson’s research.
item.description: You can participate in Parkinson's research through his foundation. They need people who don't have Parkinson's to serve as healthy controls. Periodically they send you a list of questions about your health to compare factors in people who eventually get Parkinson's vs. those who don't. Loss of smell can be an early indicator of the disease, they send you a little booklet with scratch-and-sniff pages and a multiple-choice list of what you think each one smells like. https://www.michaeljfox.org/your-role-parkinsons-research https://mysmelltest.org/pd-mjffus-gg-dir

item.title: Racism is taught, perpetuated, and inherited. Joel Bervell on racism taught in a 2015 nursing textbook
item.description: Ratified, formal, peer reviewed racism is seen today, taught as recently in 2015 (likely still taught today). There was a peer reviewed article published in 1896 by Frederick Hoffman titled "The Race Traits and Tendencies of the American Negro" which laid groundwork for hundreds of years of stereotypes, including that black people had "higher pain tolerances." Dr. Joel Bervell is an award winning medical doctor, medical mythbuster, science communicator, and advocate of iterating modern medical practices.

item.title: Here are the 50 live sites showing what’s happening in the world, organized by category
item.description: ### #Weather, #Climate & Oceans 1. **ventusky.com** → Interactive map of weather, precipitation, wind and waves 2. **earth.nullschool.net** → Global wind, ocean currents and pollution 3. **climatereanalyzer.org** → Real-time temperature anomalies 4. **nhc.noaa.gov** → Official hurricane tracking center (NOAA) 5. **tropicaltidbits.com** → Storm models side by side 6. **tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov** → Tides and water levels 7. **waterdata.usgs.gov** → Real-time river flow 8. **droughtmonitor.unl.edu** → Drought monitoring map ### Fires, Smoke & Air Quality 9. **firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov** → Active fires by satellite (NASA) 10. **fire.airnow.gov** → Smoke plume tracking 11. **aqicn.org** / **waqi.info** → Real-time air quality in cities ### Satellites, #Earth Imagery & Observation 12. **worldview.earthdata.nasa.gov** → Daily global satellite imagery (NASA) 13. **sentinel-hub.com** → Explore Sentinel satellite images 14. **nsidc.org** → Polar ice and glacier status 15. **sealevel.nasa.gov** → Sea-level change data ### #Volcanos, Earthquakes & Tsunamis 16. **volcanodiscovery.com** → Real-time volcanic activity 17. **volcano.si.edu** → Active volcanoes database 18. **emsc-csem.org** / **seismicportal.eu** → Earthquake monitoring 19. **raspberryshake.net** → Listen to seismometers live 20. **tsunami.gov** → Tsunami warning center ### Space, Auroras & Celestial Objects 21. **aurora-service.eu** → Aurora forecasts 22. **spaceweather.com** / **swpc.noaa.gov** → Space weather and solar storms 23. **heavens-above.com** / **n2yo.com** / **spotthestation.nasa.gov** → Satellite and ISS tracking 24. **theskylive.com** / **solarsystemscope.com** → Planet positions and solar system 25. **cneos.jpl.nasa.gov** → Near-Earth objects 26. **fireball.amsmeteors.org** → Meteor and fireball reports 27. **suncalc.org** → Sun path during the day 28. **lightpollutionmap.info** → Dark-sky regions ### Aviation, Traffic & Transport 29. **adsbexchange.com** / **opensky-network.org** → Live flight tracking (unfiltered / open data) 30. **openrailwaymap.org** → Worldwide railway network ### Energy & Infrastructure 31. **electricitymaps.com** → Real-time electricity mix by country 32. **energy-charts.info** → European energy production data 33. **gridwatch.co.uk** → Live UK power grid load 34. **netblocks.org** / **radar.cloudflare.com** → Internet outages and traffic ### Oceans, Animals & Biodiversity 35. **ocearch.org** → Shark tracking 36. **globalfishingwatch.org** → Global fishing fleet monitoring 37. **birdcast.info** / **ebird.org** → Bird migration and observations 38. **movebank.org** → Animal migration routes 39. **inaturalist.org** / **gbif.org** → Live biodiversity observations ### Radio & Other 40. **websdr.org** → Listen to radio receivers around the world Most of these sites remain active and reliable. They use official data from NASA, NOAA, ESA and other scientific organizations, with updates ranging from near real-time to a few hours.
